content:
Jia Chen: Heads-up — new quantized build of redwood-open-3b (q4_k) on staging shows repeated subtokens in JP outputs when we run the kuromoji tokenizer path. Not a normal hallucination, it's literal token stuttering (e.g. 'それでは、それでは、それでは').
Marcus V: :eyes: can you paste a minimal repro? Is this on translation or generation tests?
Jia Chen: repro on ja->en translation eval and also on a small generation prompt. Quick command I used:```python tools/eval.py --model redwood-open-3b-q4_k --task ja-en --split test --batch 16 --tokenizer kuromoji --quant q4```
Jia Chen: sample from the test set (ref / hyp):
- REF: "彼は昨日ここに来た。"
- HYPO (q4_k): "彼は昨日ここに来た来た来た。"
- HYPO (fp16 baseline): "彼は昨日ここに来た。"
Samir Patel: ugh. BLEU dropped on that split too?
Jia Chen: BLEU on ja-en dev: fp16 baseline 27.8 -> q4_k 19.4. chrF dropped 0.715 -> 0.662. Not all examples reproduce, ~12% of dev set has duplicated subtoken patterns.
Marcus V: sounds like a tokenization / detokenization mismatch introduced by the kuromoji path combined with quantized vocab logits. Could be rounding noise causing repeated highest-prob subtoken that corresponds to an empty joiner?
Samir Patel: is the model using SentencePiece during training? The server path here uses kuromoji to pre-tokenize before spm. Might be double-splitting edge cases (katakana elongation, punctuation U+3001).
Jia Chen: right — model was trained with spm-only pipeline. We added kuromoji as an optional pre-tokenizer last quarter for latency on mobile. I ran raw token lists from model logits vs fp16:```
FP16 tokens: [713, 2048, 98, 4001]
Q4 tokens:   [713, 2048, 2048, 98, 4001]
```
Jia Chen: so the duplication happens before detok (i.e., model emits same subtoken twice in a row), not just a detok bug.
eval-bot: automated eval summary: model redwood-open-3b-q4_k @staging — Translation ja->en: BLEU -8.4, chrF -0.053, duplicate-subtoken-rate 0.12, run 1732109876.
Marcus V: ok let's bisect: could be the quant kernel update that changed softmax tail handling. Samir, can you try running the q8 build quickly? If q8 does not reproduce, it's likely aggressive int4/q4 path.
Samir Patel: running q8 now on a 200-sample subset, will post numbers in ~10m.
Jia Chen: also adding an eval unit with a focused set of 50 jp edge cases (elongation, repeated punctuation, ZWJ, dakuten). Put it under ci/regressions/ja-subtoken-stutter.
Marcus V: good. If q8 is fine then we need to roll back the change to the q4 softmax pragmas or add a small temperature correction for q4. Also check KV cache rounding in the decoder loop.
Samir Patel: q8 results: BLEU 27.1, chrF 0.709, duplicate-subtoken-rate 0.013. Almost baseline. Jia Chen: thanks — filing ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-9876 with repro, eval logs, and sample outputs. Assigning to @marcus.
Marcus V: I'll take it. Plan: (1) reproduce locally with current q4 runtime and instrument logits to see if peak token flips due to int overflow; (2) run targeted bisect across quant kernel commits from last month; (3) add regression gate to presubmit for q4 builds.
Samir Patel: one more data point — I ran the same inputs with kuromoji disabled (spm-only) and q4 had near-baseline behavior. So the interaction is kuromoji pre-tokenization + q4 noise. Might be shape/padding differences exposing a bug.
Jia Chen: noted. For now, I'll pin staging to fp16 for ja-en experiments and update the model card. Please drop any quick hacks in the ticket rather than merging to main. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident created ML-9876 (priority P2) — assigned to Marcus V — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-9876
Marcus V: thanks all. I'll post updates in this thread after the bisect. If anyone has a quick log snippet of raw logits for the duplicated positions, paste here (just top-8 logits is fine).
